sinks.rationale: Environment.from_string compiles its source argument as a template of the configured environment — attacker text in it is expression execution on render. Position 1 is the unbound spelling (self at 0); the keyword spelling is source=.
The dominant real-world spelling is env.from_string(...) on a constructed Environment, which has no import binding to resolve; bare-name equality gated on a receiver named env, hence heuristic.
NativeEnvironment renders to native Python objects instead of text — the same from_string surface with a wider post-render blast radius, worth its own import spelling.
Engine.from_string(template_code) is Django's constructor-level compile of raw template text, reachable without the django.template.Template spelling the core pack already claims.
Tornado templates embed Python expressions; constructing one from attacker text (positional or template_string=) executes those expressions on generate().
Bottle's SimpleTemplate lines and inline blocks are Python; a template built from attacker source (positional or source=) is code execution on render.
bottle.template renders its first argument directly when it is not the name of a template file — the one-call string-render spelling of the SimpleTemplate surface.

Cheetah compiles the template source into a Python class at construction — attacker template text IS generated code, so the entry carries the code-generation CWE while pairing under the template class.
Chameleon page templates evaluate python: expressions in TAL attributes; a PageTemplate built from attacker text executes them on render.
